text:
kevin: Heads-up — embed-queue-depth alert is firing non-stop during the canary. Can we get a short mute (30m) while we watch? Also where should I pull the consumer logs/traces to prove it's canary noise?

natalie: On it. Grafana panel: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/abc123/embed-pipeline?orgId=1
Kibana logs: https://logs.redwood.ai/app/discover#/view/embed-consumer
Alert rule looks like: `sum(rate(embed_queue_depth[5m])) by (pool) > 100` — seems like a spike from the canary. I'd prefer a 20m mute, or bump threshold to 150 for 1hr if we want more breathing room.

maria: +1 to temporary mute. Suggest 30m mute + a short-term threshold bump to 140 as a middle ground. If you only want to ignore the canary, add `pool!="canary"` to the query.

kevin: Thanks. Natalie, can you create the mute and drop the ticket link here? I'll attach traces from the canary instance (x-ray trace id will be in the logs).

natalie: Done — scheduled a temporary silence for 20 minutes in Alertmanager: https://ops.redwood.ai/snoozes/CHG-4521 :white_check_mark:  Ticket: RND-3221.
Command I used:
```
reliabilityctl silence add --alert embed_queue_depth --until +20m --note "canary spike, short mute requested by kevin"
```

oncall-bot: Snooze created by natalie — expires in 20 minutes. Reminder scheduled at 5 minutes before expiration.

kevin: Great, I'll attach the traces and post back if it keeps spiking. :thumbsup:

maria: Also opened a tiny PR to make the alert more canary-aware (adds `pool!="canary"` as an option) — https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/789. If we want to keep alerting on other pools, we can merge after the canary window.

kevin: Perfect. Will verify after mute expires and update the ticket. Thanks all!
